A +/-6-hour fallback bound two ordinary rounds' findings to each other, which breaks Settled Decision 9's named round and would have David reading round N's account describing round N+1.

Comparing a marker's 7-40 character SHA against the full head SHA makes a clean pass read as having pushed, defeating Settled Decision 4's no-findings/no-push skip and buying a dispatch that should not happen.

Settled Decision 3 specifies the diff from the reviewed commit to the head, and three-dot semantics do not produce it once a permitted --force-with-lease rewrite leaves the reviewed commit off the head's ancestry.
A threads collection captured before the pass holds none of that round's findings, so the round would be translated or skipped as clean — a wrong account David has no way to doubt.

Capturing another repository's same-numbered PR is named in the threat model's own worked example as a mistake the identity checks exist to catch ('Capturing the wrong PR's snapshot because every repository has a #7'), so it is inside the model rather than outside it.

The published recipe ran in the foreground and created no exit file while the surrounding prose required both, so following it as written blocks the loop or leaves close-out with no completion signal.

A delivery failure after the model ran escaped the catch and printed neither fixed notice, so Product Intent 2's one derived chat line per round was not produced on exactly the path that most needs one.
The recipe redirected stdout where the assembler requires --out, so following it creates an empty snapshot and the dispatch can only report a parse failure.

A one-time HEAD check cannot pin what a detached, long-running role reads from a live tree, so the brief asserted an evidence boundary the code did not hold; the increment's answer was to drop Read entirely.
Multi-line provider errors inserted verbatim into the notice break Product Intent 2's single line that the builder pastes verbatim.
The fleet-wide contract still described a Read guarantee and a HEAD check that the same PR had already removed, so every consumer would read a mechanism that does not exist.
Product Intent 1 promises an account of every round, and waiting only on the stopping round's exit file lets the merge ask go out with an earlier round absent from the page.
An argument failure threw before the handler that owes David a fixed recognisable line, leaving the log's last line a raw diagnostic the skill requires to be pasted verbatim.
An unbounded lower-bound-only comment window puts round N+1's conversation under round N's heading on the catch-up case this record explicitly supports.

Settled Decision 9's single freshness comparison was wrong at GitHub's second granularity, producing the false 'unanswered' translation the check exists to prevent.
The workflow the increment itself documents detaches every round, so two overlapping deliveries can leave Product Intent 2's single page missing a completed round.

Overlapping capture pages are a supported input shape, and an undeduplicated thread root numbers one finding twice, so the account states a finding count that disagrees with every mechanical count of the same round.
Bounding the comment window at the next pass while leaving the diff endpoint at the live head was half a fix: the brief would credit a later round's code to the earlier round.

A non-atomic receipt write can be read half-formed by a concurrent delivery, turning a completed, paid-for translation into 'translation unpublished'.

Unquoted $PWD/$D inside a double-quoted bash -c is the escaping class this repository has already measured (issue #11), and here it means the dispatch never starts in a consumer checkout whose path contains a space.
